summary.oneLiner: Eastern India's largest maize wet-miller just doubled crushing capacity to 1,650 TPD and added higher-margin derivative lines (liquid glucose, maltodextrin, dextrose) — the FY27 story is operating-leverage + value-added mix shift from ~3% to ~35% of revenue, set against softening maize prices; near-term visibility is deliberately undisclosed pending plant stabilization.

thesis (one line): Eastern India's largest maize wet-miller just doubled crushing capacity to 1,650 TPD and added higher-margin derivative lines (liquid glucose, maltodextrin, dextrose) — the FY27 story is operating-leverage + value-added mix shift from ~3% to ~35% of revenue, set against softening maize prices; near-term visibility is deliberately undisclosed pending plant stabilization.
scorecard (fy26 full-year unless noted;:
| Metric | FY26 | YoY / note |
|---|---|---|
| **Operating income** | INR 1,134.2 cr | +23.9% YoY; Q4 FY26 = INR 244.6 cr |
| **Value-added (gross VA)** | INR 295.8 cr | +18% YoY |
| **Operating EBITDA** | INR 126.6 cr; margin 11.2% (FY26) | Q4 EBITDA INR 32.5 cr, margin 13.3% (up from 10.7% in Q3); margin lift = better realizations, partly offset by higher freight + more March shutdown days |
| **PAT (reported)** | INR 55.6 cr; margin 4.9% (FY26) | Q4 PAT INR 16.5 cr, margin 6.8% (sequential improvement) |
| **PAT (normalized)** | ~same; no large explicit one-offs flagged | FY26 hit by ramp-up costs ahead of expansion commissioning + higher shutdown days in March (one-offs depressing Q4 absolute EBITDA) |
| **Volume** | 2.65 lakh tons sold (FY26) | manufacturing turnover ~INR 800 cr at ~825 TPD (rest is/was trading) |
| **Realization** | Co-products (germ/gluten/fibre) realizations up "hugely" Q4→Q1; starch realization up on export market reopening | maize→starch value-add higher than last year |
| **Net debt** | ~INR 545.65 cr | Net debt/equity improved to 1.1x (from 1.9x FY25) |
| **Cash conversion cycle** | 50 days | improved from 93 days FY25 (lower inventory + receivable days) |
| **Dividend** | INR 0.25/share recommended | subject to shareholder approval |

**One-offs / distortions to flag explicitly:**
- Q4/FY26 EBITDA absolute depressed by **pre-commissioning ramp-up costs** for the expansion and **higher shutdown days in March '26**.
- Higher **freight & forwarding** costs within other expenses offset part of margin gain.
- Analyst (Keshav Garg, Counter Cyclical) challenged that QoQ operating margin fell ~19%→14% (incl. traded goods); mgmt countered that **operating EBITDA margin rose 10.7%→13.3% QoQ** and value-add increased — discrepancy due to ramp-up costs + traded-goods accounting.
- FY27 net/total debt expected to rise to ~INR 700–750 cr (incl. working-capital/CC) due to remaining capex.
guidance (critical) — **explicitly withh:
Management repeatedly and deliberately refused formal guidance ("any attempt to extract a guidance is futile now"), to come between Q1 and Q2 FY27 (by end-H1 FY27) after plant stabilizes. The few quantified directional comments given:
- **Volume / revenue:** at full 1,650 TPD utilization, revenue expected to "**at least double**" the ~INR 800 cr manufacturing base (raw-material-led, so moves with maize price). FY26 volume base = 2.65 lakh tons.
- **Value-added mix:** rising from ~**2–3% (FY26)** to ~**20–25% in FY27** (ramp year) and ~**35% at full peak capacity (FY28/next year)**.
- **VA pricing premium:** value-added delta ~**20–25% over starch prices**.
- **Margin:** no formal number; mgmt expects **"double engine" margin accretion** (economies of scale from brownfield doubling + value-added mix) from ~Q2/Q3 FY27 onward.
- **Capex:** total revised to ~INR 540 cr (from ~INR 430 cr); INR 401 cr spent by 31-Mar-26; ~INR 140 cr remaining in FY27.
- **Utilization:** mgmt expects to reach ~100% rated capacity "fairly quickly" ("weeks, not months"), citing past ramp track record.
demand / pipeline:
- End-markets: food & beverages, pharma, paper & packaging, textiles, adhesives, animal nutrition — diversified across domestic + export.
- **345 customers** as of Mar-26 (134 onboarded during FY26); dealer channel = 65.5% of annual revenue.
- **Secured a sizeable export order** during the period — strengthens near-term export revenue visibility; positioning improved by softening RM prices boosting global cost competitiveness.
- Focus on **South-East Asian** export markets for maize derivatives; export market reopening lifted starch prices.
segment (starch / derivatives / co-produ:
- Pre-expansion mix (of 825 TPD output): ~**65% native starch**, ~**30% maize by-products** (germ/gluten/fibre — natural consequence of wet milling), ~**2–3% value-added**.
- New expansion deliberately skewed toward value-added: "a large part of increased capacity feeds value-added products"; native starch delta will be modest, most delta into VA.
- Co-products (germ, gluten, fibre, steep liquor, enriched fibre) feed animal nutrition & food; realizations rose sharply.
growth / optionality:
- **Modified-starch range expansion:** cationic starch, carboxymethyl starch, pre-gel starch, spray starch, hydrol, gulal (white-labelled).
- **Derivatives:** liquid glucose (180 TPD) + maltodextrin powder (50 TPD) commissioned May-26; dextrose anhydrous (DAH), dextrose monohydrate (DMH), hydrol to come Q3–Q4 FY27.
- **White-labelling:** started with 1 company, now 4 enrolled; volume ~2–2.5% of starch qty (~6,500 units), expected to rise considerably within H1; also white-labelling gulal.
- **Exports:** building international footprint, esp. SE Asia; "One Star Export House" status.
margins & cost (maize cost):
- FY26 EBITDA margin 11.2% (Q4 13.3%); improvement from better realizations.
- **Maize cost softening:** prices down ~10% vs last year (last year hovered INR 18–23/24, ~INR 4-5 swing); delta ~INR 2/kg lower expected this year — viewed constructively but mgmt wants another quarter before structural conclusion.
- Brownfield economics: overheads won't double despite capacity doubling → operating leverage; larger procurement = better bargaining power.
- **BIIPP (Bihar policy):** interest subvention up to 10% p.a. capped at INR 20 cr over 5 years; netted against interest cost in P&L (debit receivable / credit interest cost), received within next quarter (~by June). Plus State GST reimbursement — lowers effective cost of capital.
- ~81% of FY26 electricity from captive co-gen (power capacity now 15.8 MW after +10 MW addition).
capex (capacity expansion):
- Crushing capacity scaled 825 → **1,650 TPD** (commissioned 26-May-2026); now largest maize milling facility in Eastern India.
- Scaling history: 180 TPD (FY18) → 330 (FY22) → 650 (FY24) → 750 (FY25) → 825 (FY26) → 1,650 (May-26). Revenue CAGR 32.5% FY23–FY26.
- Total capex revised UP to **~INR 540 cr** (from ~INR 430 cr) — incremental ~INR 110 cr toward expanded VA pipeline + larger co-gen. INR 401 cr spent by Mar-26; ~INR 140 cr balance in FY27.
- Power plant +10 MW (total 15.8 MW); 5 MW of new plant already drawn. 55-acre site with land for future expansion. 65,000 MT silo storage + ~240,000 t warehouse godowns.
- New facilities create ~475 direct jobs (total on-role ~950).
capital allocation (ipo proceeds):
- First call since Aug-2025 NSE/BSE listing; IPO proceeds funding the expansion.
- Net debt/equity improved 1.9x → 1.1x; CCC 50 days (from 93).
- Net debt ~INR 545.65 cr now → expected ~INR 700–750 cr total debt in FY27 (incl. working capital/CC) as capex completes.
- **Other current assets jumped INR ~45/56 cr → ~INR 150/170 cr** — due to advances to new maize suppliers + warehouses for the 1,650 TPD ramp (not a red flag per mgmt).
- Maiden dividend INR 0.25/share recommended.
- Working capital intensity: sine-curve, peaks Q1→Q2, falls Q3→Q4; CCC to range ~50–75 days.
risks:
- **Maize price volatility / monsoon:** RM is a commodity; revenue & margins move with maize prices; Bihar crop arrival delayed by rains (deliveries from ~15-16 May). Bihar is a net maize exporter so availability "never a problem."
- **Execution / ramp-up risk:** large brownfield commissioning needs stabilization; new VA lines (DAH/DMH/hydrol) phased through FY27.
- **Margin uncertainty / guidance vacuum:** mgmt withheld guidance — investors must model blind for 1-2 quarters.
- **Rising debt** during capex (to ~INR 700-750 cr).
- **Ethanol/policy ambiguity:** govt ethanol push could pull maize demand/prices either way; govt simultaneously releasing broken-rice stocks to plants (offsetting maize demand).
- **Customer concentration / competitive disclosure:** declined to break revenue by end-industry (competitive sensitivity).
mgmt tone: Confident on execution and ramp track record ("weeks not months", "double engine growth vehicle", "super substantially" VA growth) but deliberately disciplined / cautious on guidance — repeatedly resisted analyst attempts to extract numbers, framing it as prudence ("we don't want a reckless guidance"). Constructive but non-committal on maize price trajectory ("allow this to play out over another quarter"). Promotional on Bihar policy support and "largest in Eastern India" positioning.
non-obvious:
- Trading revenue (~30%+ of last year's revenue) will shrink to **near-zero** going forward — trading was historically done only to secure RM at MOQ/best deals when own requirement was low, NOT a profit center. This materially changes the revenue-mix optics (reported revenue may look softer ex-trading even as core grows).
- The 19%→14% vs 13.3% margin "dispute" with analyst hinges on whether traded goods are stripped out — clean operating EBITDA margin actually rose QoQ.
- VA shift means revenue could partially *decouple* from maize-price-driven commodity swings over time.
- Co-product realizations (germ/gluten/fibre) saw a "huge" jump Q4→Q1 — an underappreciated margin lever separate from starch.
- Mgmt couldn't split capex between native vs VA on the call (will send separately) — capital-allocation transparency gap.
challenges → beneficiaries:
- ⭐ **Import-substitution / specialty maize derivatives:** Regaal beneficiary as DAH/DMH/maltodextrin/liquid glucose capacity comes online (pharma/food/healthcare demand currently part-imported).
- ✅ **Govt maize/ethanol policy thrust + broken-rice stock release:** supports raw-material supply security for all wet-millers; Regaal benefits via Bihar location + BIIPP incentives.
- ✅ **Export-order traction (SE Asia):** softening domestic maize = improved global cost competitiveness for Indian starch exporters incl. Regaal.

themes.title: Bioenergy / Ethanol / SAF transition
themes.need: Higher ethanol-blending mandates (E20->E25/E27/E30), CBG, SAF and bio-IBA underpin a multi-year bioenergy capex cycle. PRAJIND's near-term earnings are depressed by a 1G slowdown + GenX gestation but the optionality (SAF, CBG, DC-cooling) is large; TRUALT/BALRAMCHIN/EIDPARRY/TRIVENI/GODAVARIB add ethanol/sugar; BCLIND/GULPOLY/GLOBUSSPR on grain-based distillation.
themes.driver: Higher blending-mandate notifications; SAF/CBG order conversion; sugar-cycle realisations.

themes.title: Agri value-chain - food processing, dairy, protein & seeds
themes.need: Rising protein/processed-food consumption, animal-nutrition demand and export tailwinds drive an integrated agri value-chain - DODLA/PARAGMILK on dairy; AVANTIFEED/SHINDL/SKMEGGPROD/HMAAGRO on aqua/poultry/meat protein; GODREJAGRO/KSCL/NATHBIOGEN on feed + seeds; REGAAL/SUKHJITS/GULPOLY on maize/starch; FOODSIN/MANORAMA on agri-processing & specialty fats.
themes.driver: Monsoon-led farm income; protein export demand; feed-margin recovery; festive processed-food restocking.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Eastern India's largest maize wet milling facility (1,650 TPD) in Kishanganj, Bihar, strategically located near one of India's largest maize markets and export corridors to Nepal, Bangladesh and North-East/South-East Asia.
- One of the few maize wet milling facilities in India with a Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) unit; recognized as a One Star Export House by the DGFT (Ministry of Commerce and Industry) in Fiscal 2023.
- Diversified product portfolio spanning native starch, modified starches, value-added derivatives (Liquid Glucose, Maltodextrin Powder) and co-products (germ, gluten, fiber, steep liquor) serving food, pharma, paper, textiles and animal nutrition end-markets.

growth_optionality.title: Growth / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **Modified-starch range expansion:** cationic starch, carboxymethyl starch, pre-gel starch, spray starch, hydrol, gulal (white-labelled).
- **Derivatives:** liquid glucose (180 TPD) + maltodextrin powder (50 TPD) commissioned May-26; dextrose anhydrous (DAH), dextrose monohydrate (DMH), hydrol to come Q3–Q4 FY27.
- **White-labelling:** started with 1 company, now 4 enrolled; volume ~2–2.5% of starch qty (~6,500 units), expected to rise considerably within H1; also white-labelling gulal.
- **Exports:** building international footprint, esp. SE Asia; "One Star Export House" status.

margins.title: Margins & cost (maize cost)
margins.body:
- FY26 EBITDA margin 11.2% (Q4 13.3%); improvement from better realizations.
- **Maize cost softening:** prices down ~10% vs last year (last year hovered INR 18–23/24, ~INR 4-5 swing); delta ~INR 2/kg lower expected this year — viewed constructively but mgmt wants another quarter before structural conclusion.
- Brownfield economics: overheads won't double despite capacity doubling → operating leverage; larger procurement = better bargaining power.
- **BIIPP (Bihar policy):** interest subvention up to 10% p.a. capped at INR 20 cr over 5 years; netted against interest cost in P&L (debit receivable / credit interest cost), received within next quarter (~by June). Plus State GST reimbursement — lowers effective cost of capital.
- ~81% of FY26 electricity from captive co-gen (power capacity now 15.8 MW after +10 MW addition).

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation (IPO proceeds)
capital_allocation.body:
- First call since Aug-2025 NSE/BSE listing; IPO proceeds funding the expansion.
- Net debt/equity improved 1.9x → 1.1x; CCC 50 days (from 93).
- Net debt ~INR 545.65 cr now → expected ~INR 700–750 cr total debt in FY27 (incl. working capital/CC) as capex completes.
- **Other current assets jumped INR ~45/56 cr → ~INR 150/170 cr** — due to advances to new maize suppliers + warehouses for the 1,650 TPD ramp (not a red flag per mgmt).
- Maiden dividend INR 0.25/share recommended.
- Working capital intensity: sine-curve, peaks Q1→Q2, falls Q3→Q4; CCC to range ~50–75 days.

management_tone.title: Mgmt tone
management_tone.body: Confident on execution and ramp track record ("weeks not months", "double engine growth vehicle", "super substantially" VA growth) but deliberately disciplined / cautious on guidance — repeatedly resisted analyst attempts to extract numbers, framing it as prudence ("we don't want a reckless guidance"). Constructive but non-committal on maize price trajectory ("allow this to play out over another quarter"). Promotional on Bihar policy support and "largest in Eastern India" positioning.

risks.title: Risks
risks.body:
- **Maize price volatility / monsoon:** RM is a commodity; revenue & margins move with maize prices; Bihar crop arrival delayed by rains (deliveries from ~15-16 May). Bihar is a net maize exporter so availability "never a problem."
- **Execution / ramp-up risk:** large brownfield commissioning needs stabilization; new VA lines (DAH/DMH/hydrol) phased through FY27.
- **Margin uncertainty / guidance vacuum:** mgmt withheld guidance — investors must model blind for 1-2 quarters.
- **Rising debt** during capex (to ~INR 700-750 cr).
- **Ethanol/policy ambiguity:** govt ethanol push could pull maize demand/prices either way; govt simultaneously releasing broken-rice stocks to plants (offsetting maize demand).
- **Customer concentration / competitive disclosure:** declined to break revenue by end-industry (competitive sensitivity).

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious
non_obvious.body:
- Trading revenue (~30%+ of last year's revenue) will shrink to **near-zero** going forward — trading was historically done only to secure RM at MOQ/best deals when own requirement was low, NOT a profit center. This materially changes the revenue-mix optics (reported revenue may look softer ex-trading even as core grows).
- The 19%→14% vs 13.3% margin "dispute" with analyst hinges on whether traded goods are stripped out — clean operating EBITDA margin actually rose QoQ.
- VA shift means revenue could partially *decouple* from maize-price-driven commodity swings over time.
- Co-product realizations (germ/gluten/fibre) saw a "huge" jump Q4→Q1 — an underappreciated margin lever separate from starch.
- Mgmt couldn't split capex between native vs VA on the call (will send separately) — capital-allocation transparency gap.

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries
challenges.body:
- ⭐ **Import-substitution / specialty maize derivatives:** Regaal beneficiary as DAH/DMH/maltodextrin/liquid glucose capacity comes online (pharma/food/healthcare demand currently part-imported).
- ✅ **Govt maize/ethanol policy thrust + broken-rice stock release:** supports raw-material supply security for all wet-millers; Regaal benefits via Bihar location + BIIPP incentives.
- ✅ **Export-order traction (SE Asia):** softening domestic maize = improved global cost competitiveness for Indian starch exporters incl. Regaal.

---

qoq_log.title: QoQ Log
qoq_log.body:
| Item | This call (Q4 FY26) |
|---|---|
| **Thesis** | Capacity doubling (1,650 TPD) + VA mix shift to ~35% peak; operating leverage story; guidance deferred to H1 FY27. |
| **Rev** | FY26 INR 1,134.2 cr (+23.9% YoY); Q4 INR 244.6 cr |
| **EBITDA/margin** | FY26 INR 126.6 cr / 11.2%; Q4 INR 32.5 cr / 13.3% (vs 10.7% Q3) |
| **PAT (rptd & norm)** | FY26 INR 55.6 cr / 4.9%; Q4 INR 16.5 cr / 6.8%; norm ~same (ramp-up costs + March shutdown one-offs) |
| **Volume + realization** | FY26 vol 2.65 lakh t; co-product & starch realizations up; maize→starch value-add higher YoY |
| **Net debt** | ~INR 545.65 cr; net D/E 1.1x (vs 1.9x); → ~INR 700-750 cr FY27 |
| **Guidance** | WITHHELD — formal outlook by end-H1 FY27. Directional: rev "at least double"; VA 20-25% FY27 → ~35% FY28; VA premium 20-25% over starch; capex INR 540 cr (INR 140 cr balance FY27) |
| **One-offs** | Pre-commissioning ramp-up costs; higher March shutdown days; higher freight; trading revenue collapsing to ~zero |
| **Key event** | 1,650 TPD + liquid glucose (180 TPD) + maltodextrin (50 TPD) + 10 MW co-gen commissioned 26-May-2026; first call post Aug-25 IPO; maiden dividend INR 0.25 |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Listing] Regaal Resources Limited (RRL) was listed on NSE and BSE on 20 August 2025.
- [Shareholding] As on 30 Jun 2026: Promoter & Promoter Group 71.3%, Retail Investors & HUF 19.5%, Others 5.8%, Institutional Investors & NBFCs 2.6%, NRIs 0.5%, FPIs 0.3%.
- [Domestic expansion] Only 0.67% of FY26 revenue came from South India; the company is targeting deeper penetration across Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana as a growth lever distinct from exports.
